text:
Functional relationships need explicit evidence. [Sugahara et al. (2024)](https://ken.ieice.org/ken/paper/202401254caa/eng/) argue that co-purchase/co-view labels are noisy proxies for complementarity and introduce function-based annotations independent of behavior. [Function-based labels for complementary recommendation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167865525003976) extends this approach with directional functional labels and human-versus-LLM annotation comparisons. Implication: distinguish functional complements, substitutes, content matches, redundancy, and unrelated items; shared topic or co-occurrence alone cannot establish compatibility.

Preference judges require calibration. [Can LLM be a Personalized Judge? (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.592/) reports low agreement with human preferences overall, with better agreement on high-certainty cases. [Tripathi et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14716) find pairwise judgments vulnerable to irrelevant distractors, so pairwise evaluation is not automatically more reliable than independent scoring. [Sage (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16041) additionally tests repeated-pair stability and preference transitivity. These findings support explicit rubrics, order swaps, repeated judgments, and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

Suggested audit design, inferred from these findings: independently annotate a small sample across all four categories using only training histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Record relation type, supporting evidence spans, recent-versus-long-term relevance, and unknown compatibility or purpose. Measure annotator agreement, order consistency, and abstention coverage; adjudicate disagreements. Treat timestamps as evidence of recency, not proof of intent, and leave diversity/conformity traits unobserved. Convert verified failures into sampling or loss hypotheses—for example, evidence-supported irrelevant hard negatives or recency weighting—then accept changes only through the pinned macro validation HR@10.
